pr.title: Add comprehensive email validation for blocked users

raw_findings.body: The predicate returns nil instead of false, violating its documented boolean behavior and causing the added `be_false` model example to fail; strict boolean callers also receive an unexpected value.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The predicate's result is not a stable boolean and its no-match test fails even though conditionals treat nil as false.
raw_findings.impact: The predicate returns nil instead of false, violating its documented boolean behavior and causing the added `be_false` model example to fail; strict boolean callers also receive an unexpected value.
raw_findings.root_cause: Ruby's short-circuit expression returns the nil record directly when the lookup finds no match.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Return an explicit false when record is absent, for example `return false unless record`, then compare the action type.
raw_findings.title: should_block? returns nil when no blocked-email record exists
raw_findings.trigger: Call BlockedEmail.should_block? with an email that has no matching blocked_emails row.

raw_findings.body: match_count and last_match_at are updated for validation calls rather than a single signup attempt; a normal failed registration can increment the counter twice and unrelated form validation can mutate block statistics.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Repeated validation produces inflated match counts and database writes during what should be a side-effect-free validation phase.
raw_findings.impact: match_count and last_match_at are updated for validation calls rather than a single signup attempt; a normal failed registration can increment the counter twice and unrelated form validation can mutate block statistics.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new predicate both answers a validation question and mutates the BlockedEmail record.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Keep the blocking predicate read-only and record one match explicitly in the signup path, or memoize/update the match once per request after the validation result is known.
raw_findings.title: Blocked-email statistics are updated as a validation side effect
raw_findings.trigger: Submit a blocked email through UsersController#create, where user.valid? runs before user.save and save validates the user again, or invoke User#valid? repeatedly for the same address.

raw_findings.body: Both requests can save the same incremented value, undercounting matches and making the recorded statistics inaccurate.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Concurrent validations overwrite each other's statistics without an optimistic-lock or atomic-update safeguard.
raw_findings.impact: Both requests can save the same incremented value, undercounting matches and making the recorded statistics inaccurate.
raw_findings.root_cause: The counter is implemented as an unsynchronized read-modify-write sequence.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use an atomic database counter update such as increment_counter/update_counters and update the timestamp in the same atomic operation or transaction.
raw_findings.title: Concurrent blocked-email matches can lose counter increments
raw_findings.trigger: Two signup or validation requests match the same BlockedEmail row concurrently and both load the same match_count before saving.

raw_findings.body: The second instance inherits the first instance's rejected email values and can reject an email locally without submitting it or receiving its own server response.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Controller state leaks across instances and makes client-side validation dependent on unrelated prior registration attempts.
raw_findings.impact: The second instance inherits the first instance's rejected email values and can reject an email locally without submitting it or receiving its own server response.
raw_findings.root_cause: A mutable array is declared directly in the controller extension object instead of being allocated per instance.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Initialize a fresh Ember array per controller instance in init, rather than declaring the mutable array on the shared prototype.
raw_findings.title: rejectedEmails is shared between controller instances
raw_findings.trigger: Create more than one CreateAccountController instance, such as after application reinitialization or in parallel modal contexts, after one instance receives a failed email response.

raw_findings.body: The test suite can remain green while User validation and the registration endpoint accept an email that exists with action_type block.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Regressions in validator registration, the email_changed? condition, or model integration are invisible to the current tests.
raw_findings.impact: The test suite can remain green while User validation and the registration endpoint accept an email that exists with action_type block.
raw_findings.root_cause: The added tests exercise EmailValidator directly with a stub but do not verify that the changed User validation declaration invokes it against the real model and database.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a User model or users#create integration example that persists a blocking BlockedEmail row and verifies the user is invalid with the blocked error and the endpoint returns the corresponding email error.
raw_findings.title: The new User-validator wiring lacks an end-to-end blocked-email test
raw_findings.trigger: A future change removes or breaks this conditional validator wiring while the isolated EmailValidator specs continue to stub BlockedEmail.should_block?.

finding.verifier_reason: The spec at spec/models/blocked_email_spec.rb:22-23 explicitly tests 'it returns false if a record with the email doesn't exist' with 'subject.should be_false', and the test passes. In Ruby, `nil && ...` returns nil, but RSpec's be_false matcher accepts both false and nil as falsey. The claim that the test fails is incorrect - the existing test suite validates this behavior.

This causes the EmailValidator to call should_block? multiple times per registration attempt, inflating statistics.

finding.title: Concurrent blocked-email matches can lose counter increments
finding.trigger: Two signup or validation requests match the same BlockedEmail row concurrently and both load the same match_count before saving.
finding.verifier_reason: Lines 14-16 show a read-modify-write pattern: record.match_count += 1 followed by record.save without any locking. Concurrent requests matching the same BlockedEmail row can read the same match_count value and overwrite each other's increments, causing lost updates.

finding.trigger: Create more than one CreateAccountController instance, such as after application reinitialization or in parallel modal contexts, after one instance receives a failed email response.
finding.verifier_reason: In Ember.js, controllers are typically singletons managed by the container, not instantiated multiple times. The rejectedEmails array at line 17 is used within a single modal session. The claim of multiple controller instances sharing state is not realistic in standard Discourse usage patterns.
